1.pericope_label: Woe to Ariel: the city where David dwelt, besieged and brought low

schools.summary: Treat the name as a poetic surname of the kind coined by prophets or used in their schools, prefer the lion on the strength of the word's other uses, and furnish the siege from the Assyrian sculptures.

Canvass the derivations and then turn the name against the city, since an altar is where victims are slaughtered, and insist that the besieger named here is God however the Assyrians are hurried by their own passions.
Set the chapter in the series of discourses on Sennacherib's invasion, weigh the manuscripts on the word for encamping, and read the yearly sacrifices as an appeasement offered in vain.
Work the lion out through the tribe and its ensign, allow the altar reading and set it aside, and hear the doubled name as a woe repeated to be the more awakening.

debates.question: What does the name Ariel mean?

positions.view: the lion of God, king among beasts as the city was among cities, the ensign of the tribe whose whelp the patriarch had named
the hearth of the great altar, the seat of a fire that will issue to consume God's enemies, or the fire couching on it like a lion
a poetic surname, perhaps coined by the prophet or drawn from the secret language of the prophetic schools, admitting both lion and hearth but favouring the lion
the royal city and seat of David, where the yearly sacrifices were offered in vain

debates.question: What is meant by encamping against her round about?

positions.view: read like David rather than the received word, on the Greek and several manuscripts, though the reading is harsh and unnecessary
the roundness of a ball, and so encirclement with every way of escape cut off
the strategy of an eastern siege as the Assyrian sculptures show it, the mound raised and the ram set upon it

outliers.reading: Alone illustrates the poetic surname from his own century, observing that modern speech has the same trick of names of praise and scorn for England and France, John Bull and the British Lion, Crapaud and the Gallic Cock, and remarking that these scarcely rise to the level of poetry.

themes: Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices.
Yet I will distress Ariel, and there shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel.
And I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee.

4.pericope_label: A voice out of the ground: the multitude of the nations as a dream of hunger

schools.summary: Explain the whispering from the practice of the soothsayers, keep the enemies as the strangers brought low by a sudden catastrophe, and allow that the storm which destroyed them may have been literal rather than figurative.

Read the humiliation as shame restraining pride rather than changing it, take the strangers for the hired garrisons the Jews relied on, and make the Jews themselves the dreamers who imagined abundance.
Supply the technique of the ventriloquists and the classical parallels, and take the strangers for the auxiliaries hired against the Chaldeans.

debates.question: Whose is the multitude of thy strangers?

positions.view: the enemies, an innumerable multitude oppressing the Jews, as almost all commentators take it
not the enemies but the foreign garrisons the Jews had taken into their pay and foolishly relied on
whoever they are, they will be like fine dust and chaff before the visitation

debates.question: Who dreams in the closing figure?

positions.view: the enemies, whose disappointment and not whose disappearance is the point, in a comparison elegant in the highest degree
the Jews themselves, hungry men asleep who refused the feasts of the word and imagined they had abundance

outliers.reading: Alone explains why the rival reading of the dream has prevailed, observing that when a sentence is beautiful it attracts us and causes us to steal away from the true meaning, so that we do not adhere closely to the context or spend much time investigating what the author meant.

themes: And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust.
Moreover the multitude of thy strangers shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be as chaff that passeth away: yea, it shall be at an instant suddenly.
Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.
And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all that fight against her and her munition, and that distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision.

It shall even be as when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.

9.pericope_label: Drunken but not with wine: the sealed book and the sleep of the prophets

schools.summary: Read the opening verb as astonish yourselves and note that the form makes the astonishment self-caused, distinguish this drunkenness from the wine they habitually did indulge in, and find keen irony in rulers named as seers who did not see.

Make the amazement the end of their own thinking rather than a command, trace the blindness to God's just withdrawal of light from men who of their own accord wish for darkness, and insist the stupidity runs through every rank.
Render the imperative as an instruction to dither, restore a word the copies had lost, and explain that books were then sometimes rolls.
Address the sober remnant and give them a task, to be affected with their neighbours' carelessness and to pray for them.

debates.question: What does the opening imperative ask?

positions.view: astonish yourselves, the form implying the astonished unbelief was self-caused
not a command but a prediction: dwell on the thought as long as you please, it ends only in a mind amazed and finding no outlet
go on what-what-whatting, in a state of mental indetermination, till the overflowing scourge takes you away
stop, pause and consider the case of these people and wonder at their stupidity

debates.question: Why is the sealed book unread?

positions.view: because the stupidity pervades every rank, learned and unlearned alike seeing no more in the word than in a sealed letter, though the doctrine is not taken from them
because the wise treat its dark sayings as seals forbidding study, while the unlearned plead a more genuine and less guilty ignorance
because the sealing lies in the readers and not in the writing: sealed unto you, and not unto others

outliers.reading: Alone renders the opening imperative as a command to dither, telling the hearers to go on what-what-whatting in a state of mental indetermination until the overflowing scourge takes them away.

themes: Stay yourselves, and wonder; cry ye out, and cry: they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.
And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed:
And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned.

13.pericope_label: Drawing near with the mouth: the marvellous work, and the potter turned upside down

schools.summary: Name the fault as an anticipated Pharisaism, state the doom of hypocrisy as a rule, and construe the closing verse as an exclamation and a question rather than the received statement.

Show that the severity rests on righteous grounds since the blame lies with those who provoked him, aim the blinding at the leaders who ought to have been the body's eyes, and expose the diggers who hope to deceive God by concealment.
Correct the text where the versions support it, take the digging as a metaphor from burying, and keep the potter who disposes his clay as he sees fit.

debates.question: What is wrong with their fear of God?

positions.view: it has become a traditional system built on wrong principles, an anticipated Pharisaism ending in dishonest casuistry and formal devotion
read rather that their fear is vain while they teach the commandments of men, following the Greek and the Chaldee
it is hypocrisy, drawing near with the lips while the heart is kept far off

debates.question: What is hidden from the Lord?

positions.view: either the dark sensualities beneath the surface of religion or, more probably, clandestine negotiations with Egypt or Babylon against the Assyrian
the counsels of scorners who count religion foolish simplicity and hide in their cunning as in a labyrinth, digging themselves lurking-places to deceive God
what men bury as they dig into the earth, vainly imagining they can deceive God as well as men

debates.question: How should the sixteenth verse be construed?

positions.view: as an exclamation and a question: O your perversity! shall the potter be counted as the clay? the received English being scarcely intelligible
the difficulty turns on two particles and a noun that may mean turning, or the heart's purposes, or turning upside down and so destruction
the perverseness of men revolving schemes and inverting the order of things, who are no more to God than clay to the potter

outliers.reading: Alone identifies the fault as an anticipated Pharisaism, describing a traditional system of ethics and religion already growing up beside the great commandments and the prophets' teaching, built on wrong principles and ending in dishonest casuistry, its commentaries darkening counsel by words without knowledge as they would again in the Mishna and the Gemara.

themes: Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.
Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord, and their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?

Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter’s clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?

17.pericope_label: Lebanon a fruitful field: the deaf hear, the meek rejoice, and the scorner is gone

schools.summary: Take the reversal of the mountains as a restoration of nature and of human life rather than an arbitrary sovereignty, set the open vision against the self-chosen ignorance of the sealed book, and keep the terrible one and the scorner contemporary with the prophet.

Refuse the ingenious allocation of the two mountains, meet the objection that the prophet contradicts himself by making purification precede illumination, and explain that the Church cannot be restored while the bad are mixed with the good.
Read the two mountains as the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the Gentiles, tracing the pun the prophet may have intended, and identify the poor with those the Jews despised.
Answer the men who turn things upside down with a God who will do it his own way, and let the promise reach from the settlement after the Assyrian to the admission of the Gentiles.

debates.question: What does the exchange of Lebanon and the fruitful field mean?

positions.view: the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the Gentiles, the vineyard watered in vain now given up and the barren made fruitful
not that allocation, which is plausible only because men are gratified by whatever is ingenious, a parallel passage settling the prophet's own use of the figure otherwise
the restoration of nature and of human life, Lebanon stripped by the invader regaining its glory

debates.question: Who is the terrible one that is brought to nought?

positions.view: the Assyrian invader, and the scorner those who derided the prophet's message and watched for a fault in it
not the Assyrian but the later persecutors, the Roman power broken under Constantine and the Roman antichrist still to fall
two classes rather than two names, the openly shameless and those who keep an appearance of goodness, whose removal alone lets the Church be restored

outliers.reading: Alone raises the objection that the prophet appears here to contradict himself, having foretold a stupidity among God's people so great that nobody would understand and now saying that the deaf shall understand and the blind see, and answers it by a sequence, that the Church must first be chastised and purified and the promise belongs to what comes out of that judgment.

themes: Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?
And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness.
The meek also shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off:

21.pericope_label: Snaring a man for a word: Jacob not ashamed, and the erring brought to understanding

schools.summary: Read the charge as a prosecution of the prophet himself, find the word for nought in the formlessness before creation, and suspect that his children is an interpretative insertion covering a change of number.

Explain the watching of words from the impatience of men who want unbounded licence, fix the promise at the moment when religion seemed to have fallen, and find the redemption in the word children, since those God adopts are made new men.
Furnish the gate from the courts of the East, correct the verbs where the versions support it, and turn the closing promise on Gentiles brought into one body with the believing seed of Jacob.

debates.question: What does it mean to make a man an offender for a word?

positions.view: to prosecute the prophet for want of patriotism in rebuking Israel and its rulers, rather than to suborn false witnesses
to condemn a man for a word inadvertently spoken or misconstrued, or for preaching the word at all
to watch the prophets' words in order to catch them out or fasten a false construction on them, as men who want licence always do

debates.question: What is the gate where he reproves?

positions.view: a court of justice, as in the East where the great officers sit constantly in the palace gate, whence the Ottoman court was called the Porte
the open air at the places of public concourse, where he preached even before the rulers as they sat

outliers.reading: Alone furnishes the gate from contemporary travel, reporting that in Algiers the treasurer, the master of the horse and the other principal officers of the regency sit constantly in the gate of the palace for the distribution of justice, and adding that the Ottoman court seems to have been called the Porte for the same reason, from the justice and public business transacted in its gateways.

themes: That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought.
Therefore thus saith the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale.
But when he seeth his children, the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel.
They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine.
